changes: Security: links to encrypted rooms now say so, and Bellion refuses to join, rejoin or resume such a room if the server claims it isn't encrypted.
Security: when someone leaves while you were reconnecting, the room's encryption keys change, as they do when someone leaves normally.
Security: Bellion opens a Discord page in your browser only right after you click Connect Discord, and it no longer stays connected to the server for Discord unless you linked it.
Security: opening a port on your router only talks to your router.
After a crash, Bellion asks before sending the end of its log, and reports are anonymous by default. Gear > Crash reports changes this.
Windows: your identity key and the passwords of recent rooms are now protected with your Windows account.
Gear > Your identity key... can back up your identity key to a file with a passphrase and restore it on another computer, so you keep your tag and the hosted rooms you own.
The download now includes the licenses of everything Bellion Share is built with.
In a call, a new QR code button under the People list shows your room's link as a QR code, so a phone can join by scanning it.
Screen sharing: a change on your screen, like the next slide, now reaches viewers right away, even when nothing else moves.
Screen sharing no longer lowers its resolution when your screen is simply not changing much.
Clearer dialogs: buttons now say what they do, like Leave and Stay, and Send logs confirms properly.
Video windows no longer flash black when a 60 fps stream starts.
Screen sharing no longer keeps lowering its resolution when that doesn't help: if a lower resolution isn't faster, Bellion goes back to the one you chose and stays there.
New option under Share options > Advanced: Keep my chosen resolution, so Bellion never lowers it when your computer seems slow.
Windows: 60 fps screen shares now capture up to 60 frames a second, not 30.
Windows: screen sharing now resizes the picture on the graphics card, so large screens share more smoothly.
Windows: fixed a crash when a video window opened or switched to 60 fps, for example when watching a 4K stream.
Names and notes on videos are now drawn by Bellion itself, on a soft dark panel.
Check for updates now always answers, also when you already have the newest version.
When an update fails to install, Bellion now writes down why, and Help > Send logs includes it, so we can fix it faster.
Linux: updates no longer ask for your password. Bellion now keeps its own copy in your home folder and updates it there, and goes back to the version you had if an update doesn't start properly.
Linux: like on Windows, Bellion installs a waiting update as it starts, with a small window you can skip.
After an update, Bellion shows which build it updated to once, instead of a bare "updated" and then the same note again at the next start.

Updates have their own button between the settings gear and the help button; a dot shows when one is ready. The bar at the top now only appears for a required update, a download in progress, or a problem.
On Windows, Bellion installs a waiting update as it starts, with a small window you can skip. If the new version doesn't start properly, you're back on the one you had.
Updates found while Bellion is open are downloaded in the background when you're not in a call, so they're ready for the next start.
Stopping your share now stops its sound too. You can still share sound on its own.
4K streams now load: their picture could fail to appear.
When your computer briefly can't keep up at the start, Bellion no longer drops you to a lower quality for good, and it tries your chosen quality again later.
Bellion opens where you left it, at the same size, after an update or restart.
The scroll bar under the quality choices no longer covers them.
The volume slider on a video moves again when you click or drag it, and the other buttons on that bar update again.
Each person has a speaker next to the eye: click it to mute them for you. It lights up while they talk, and shows when they send no audio.
Sounds and auto-watch moved from the settings menu to buttons at the bottom right of the call: the music note, and the eye with play or stop.
Including voice chat apps in whole-system audio is now a checkbox under Whole system in Share options.
Buttons show a tooltip when you rest the mouse on them.
Discord: connect your account once in the browser and Bellion Share follows your voice channel. Discord doesn't need to run on this computer.
The connection to the Bellion Share server accepts only certificates from its public authorities, so a company proxy or antivirus can't read it. Your own servers can be pinned too (Servers...).
After an update, Bellion Share shows what changed. Help > What's new shows it any time.
A new update shows its changes for 30 seconds when it's found.
Updates no longer fail on slow connections, and the banner shows download progress.
Whole-system audio leaves out voice chat apps (Discord, TeamSpeak...), so others in the voice call don't hear voices twice. Settings can include them.
Closing a stream window closes it and stops that stream, sound too. The eye brings it back.
Fixes smeared video that wouldn't recover.
Video windows show 60 fps streams at 60.
A 4K60 share the encoder can't keep up with steps down instead of silently halving the frame rate.
Windows: Bellion Share keeps full speed behind a fullscreen game.
Stops a log flood while sharing and watching.
Fixes shared sound going silent on Linux after about half a second (viewers heard nothing).
Adds a Test tone audio option to check that others hear you, plus audio diagnostics in logs.
